title: Unique identifier in geofencing notifications
description: Geofencing notifications may contain unique identifiers (e.g., device ID, user ID) that can be used to link data to specific individuals across different systems or contexts.

title: Quasi-identifier through location and timing data
description: Combination of location data (zone entry/exit) and timestamp can serve as quasi-identifiers that may uniquely identify individuals when combined with other available information.

title: Revealing attributes in location data
description: Geofencing data includes revealing attributes such as precise location, time of entry/exit, and zone definitions that can support identification of the data subject.

title: Sensitive location data collection
description: Location data is highly sensitive personal data that may be collected beyond what is strictly functionally required for simple geofencing notifications.

title: Data propagation to external entity
description: Geofencing data is propagated from Process P2 to ExternalEntity EE1, potentially exposing data to parties beyond the immediate functional need.

title: Unawareness of location tracking
description: Data subjects (children) may not be aware that their location is being continuously monitored and that notifications are being generated and sent to external entities.

title: Lack of control over data processing preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences regarding how, when, and for how long their location data is processed and shared.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing location data and generating notifications may exceed what is actually needed for the stated functional goal of geofencing alerts.

title: Linking through unique identifier in location history
description: Location history data stored in DS1 may contain unique identifiers (user IDs, device IDs) that can be used to link data records to specific individuals across different contexts or systems.

title: Quasi-identifier combining in location history
description: Location history data contains multiple attributes (timestamps, locations, routes) that can serve as quasi-identifiers. When combined, these attributes can uniquely identify individuals even without explicit identifiers.

title: Profiling individual through location patterns
description: Location history data can be analyzed to identify patterns in individual behavior, movements, and routines, enabling profiling that links data to specific individuals.

title: Processing of identified location data
description: The system processes location history data which is identified personal data, directly linking to specific data subjects.

title: Revealing attributes in location data
description: Location history data contains revealing attributes (home address, workplace, frequent locations) that support identification of the data subject.

title: System response reveals location data existence
description: The map/history view served by P1 reveals that location data exists and is accessible, potentially exposing the existence of sensitive personal data.

title: Sensitive data type collected
description: Location history is highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected and processed when strictly required for the functional purpose.

title: Excessive amount of location data processed
description: Full location history may be processed beyond what is functionally needed for displaying a map/history view, potentially including unnecessary historical data points.

title: Unnecessary treatment and analysis of location data
description: Location data may be further analyzed, enriched, or transformed in ways not necessary to achieve the functionality of displaying the map/history view.

title: Excessive duration/retention of location data
description: Location history may be stored longer than functionally needed, increasing the risk of unauthorized access or misuse over time.

title: Unawareness of location data processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their location history is being retrieved, processed, and displayed in the map/history view.

title: Lack of control over location data preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their location data is processed, stored, and displayed.

title: Lack of control for rectification/erasure
description: Data subjects may lack control to rectify incorrect location data or remove personal data that is no longer relevant.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More location data is processed than is actually needed for the functional purpose of displaying the map/history view.

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Location history data may be stored longer than needed, violating the storage limitation principle of GDPR.

title: Linking through unique identifier in location data
description: Child's location data can be linked to the specific child through unique identifiers (e.g., device ID, user account), enabling tracking of the child's movements across contexts.

title: Quasi-identifier combining location with other attributes
description: Location data combined with other attributes (time, location type, family relationships) can serve as quasi-identifiers to uniquely identify the child.

title: Processing of identified location data
description: The Mobile App Backend processes identified location data of the child, which directly reveals the child's whereabouts.

title: Sensitive location data shared
description: Live location data is highly sensitive personal data that should only be shared when strictly required. Sharing real-time location with a secondary guardian may exceed functional necessity.

title: Excessive location granularity
description: Live location data is disclosed at a very fine-grained level (real-time coordinates), which may be more detailed than functionally needed for guardian access.

title: Data propagation to external party
description: Location data is propagated to an external entity (Secondary Guardian) where it may not be strictly needed, increasing exposure risk.

title: Predetermined party data sharing
description: Location data is shared with a predetermined set of parties (secondary guardian), which is known at design time but still represents data exposure to external entities.

title: Child unawareness of location sharing
description: The child (data subject) may not be aware that their live location is being shared with a secondary guardian, violating transparency requirements.

title: Lack of child control over location sharing
description: The child may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding who can access their live location data.

title: Potential data minimization violation
description: Sharing live location data may process more personal data than actually needed, potentially violating GDPR data minimization principle.

title: Potential invalid consent for location sharing
description: Consent for sharing child's live location with secondary guardian may not be valid if not properly obtained, informed, or age-appropriate.

title: Location data linked to child identity
description: Live location data can be linked to a specific child through identifiers, enabling tracking and association of location with individual identity.

title: Processing of identified location data
description: The system processes identified personal data (child's live location) which contains information that can identify the data subject.

title: Quasi-identifier combining in aggregated analytics
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics shared with advertising partner may contain quasi-identifiers (e.g., device IDs, usage patterns, time stamps) that can be combined with external data to re-identify individuals.
assumptions: Analytics data may retain enough attributes to enable re-identification when combined with other data sources.
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty about the exact granularity of 'aggregated' data - if properly anonymized, risk would be lower.

title: Profiling through analytics data
description: Usage and engagement analytics can be analyzed to create user profiles, potentially linking data back to specific individuals through behavioral patterns.
assumptions: Advertising/analytics partner may use the data for profiling purposes beyond the stated purpose.
uncertainty_note: Depends on partner's data usage policies and technical capabilities.

title: Quasi-identifiers in analytics metadata
description: Analytics data may contain combinations of attributes (e.g., app usage frequency, feature interactions, session duration) that serve as quasi-identifiers enabling identification of data subjects.
assumptions: Aggregated data may still retain identifying characteristics through attribute combinations.
uncertainty_note: Assuming 'aggregated' does not mean fully anonymized - if truly anonymized, this threat would not apply.

title: Data propagation to external analytics partner
description: Personal data is propagated to an external advertising/analytics partner where it may be accessible beyond the functional requirements of the app's free tier funding.
assumptions: The external partner may have broader access to the data than necessary for the stated purpose.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the partner's data handling practices and contractual safeguards.

title: Data shared with predetermined external party
description: Analytics data is shared with a known, predetermined external party (advertising/analytics partner) which expands the exposure of personal data beyond the app's internal processing.
assumptions: The advertising partner is a known third party with access to personal data.
uncertainty_note: This is inherent to the flow design - the risk level depends on partner trustworthiness.

title: User unawareness of data sharing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their usage and engagement analytics are being shared with external advertising/analytics partners.
assumptions: Privacy policies may not clearly communicate this data sharing, or users may not read/understand them.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the app's privacy notice clarity and user engagement with it.

title: Lack of user control over data sharing preferences
description: Users may lack control to opt-out of analytics data sharing with advertising partners, or to customize which data is shared.
assumptions: No granular consent mechanism exists for analytics data sharing.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the app's consent management implementation.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data may be processed and shared than is actually needed to fund the app's free tier, as aggregated analytics may contain more detail than functionally required.
assumptions: The data sharing exceeds what is strictly necessary for the stated purpose.
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether the analytics are truly minimal or if they include unnecessary attributes.

title: Potential invalid consent for analytics data sharing
description: Analytics data sharing may rely on consent that is not valid (e.g., not freely given, not informed, or bundled with other terms).
assumptions: Consent mechanisms for analytics sharing may not meet GDPR validity requirements.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the specific consent implementation and legal review of the app's privacy practices.
